The Cameron Highlanders - Scott Skinner composition

This is originally a Scott Skinner march which has four parts. It is called The Cameron HighlanderS. Again, the setting has changed now that it has ben absorbed into the Irish tradition but it is recognisably the same tune.

John

Re: The Cameron Highlander

Possibly a Pipe March although it was written by Scott Skinner.

↳ Posted by Connor Hickey on November 26th, 2019.

Re: The Cameron Highlanders

The Cameron Highlanders was the regiment in which Sandy Skinner - James Scott Skinner’s brother - served for 11 years. Classed as a “quick march”.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on November 26th, 2019.

The Cameron Highlanders, X:8

Here’s the J. Scott Skinner tune which is called “Cameron’s Quickstep, or Henderson’s March”.

I think it’s supposed to be in 2/4 but I put it in 4/4 so that the “play audio” sounds better.

↳ Posted by Richard D Cook on April 16th, 2021.

Re: The Cameron Highlanders

BTW the “Camerons” were a Highland clan, and a Highland regiment, and had nothing to do with the “Cameronians” which were a religious sect, and a Rifles regiment.

↳ Posted by Richard D Cook on April 16th, 2021.

Yet another name - Mick Mulcahy’s

Obviously not correct, but a slight variation of this tune is travelling under the alias “Mick Mulcahy’s”. I’ve added that name here to make it easier for others who have been so misdirected to hunt it down!

↳ Posted by Tania_O on August 21st, 2025.

Re: The Cameron Highlanders

Skinner called this a quickstep, not a march. He played it straight (many pipers play it like an 2/4 march with lots of swing) and at a fair tempo of around 118bpm.

Here’s the original printed notation on Aberdeen University’s Skinner page - https://www.abdn.ac.uk/scottskinner/display.php?ID=JSS0804

And here’s a recording of Skinner himself playing the tune. https://www.abdn.ac.uk/scottskinner/music/cd116b.mp3

↳ Posted by bagpie on January 26th, 2026.
